Section 1 of the bill directs the Secretary of the Interior 
to convey to Theresa Brost, without consideration, all right, title 
and interest of the United States and the Fort Peck Indian Tribes in 
440 acres of land. Section 2 of the bill provides that the conveyance 
is to be subject to any existing lease. Section 3 authorizes the 
Secretary of the Interior to negotiate with the Fort Peck Tribes to 
determine what amount should be paid for the Tribes’ interest in the 
lands, and to deposit such amount in the Treasury to the credit of 
the Tribes. The bill makes no provision for an appropriation of such 
amount.
Your Committee has requested a report on S. 327, a bill 
"Directing the Secretary of the Interior to convey certain land 
situated in the State of Montana to Theresa Brost.”
The lands consist of the home stead entries of Nicholas A. 
Brost (Great Falls 054270) and of Charles A. Brost (Great Falls 
055278). The entry of Nicholas was allowed on January 21, 1916; 
the entry of Charles was allowed on April 25, 1917, and amended on 
June 6, 1921. Except for the original deposit of 20 percent at the 
time of entry, only one token payment was subsequently made on 
October 20, 1927. In November 1932, Theresa E. Brost and William C. 
Brost advised the Bureau of Land Management that they were the trans­
ferees of both entries. The Congress enacted various relief statutes 
extending the time for payments, all of which have long since expired. 
The Brosts were regularly notified of the effects of these acts and 
urged to comply with the provisions thereof, and, in each instance, 
except on the occasion of the October 20, 1927 payment, the Brosts 
replied by filing an appeal and request for further extension. 
The entries were canceled on June 10, 1940.
